title: 3FACE
media: Online / net art | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: An edition of 4,096 NFT artworks on the Ethereum blockchain, released through the platform Outland. Each 3FACE reads its owner's wallet and public transaction history, interprets it through a personality model of Nature, Nurture and Posture developed by Cheng, and renders a generative portrait; the owner can update the reading as the wallet accrues more history. MoMA and the Whitney Museum acquired editions in 2023.

title: 3SDC (Sunlight, Soil & Shit (De)Cycle)
artist: Oron Catts, Ionat Zurr & Steve Berrick
media: Material / sculpture | Sensor / interaction | Network / data
summary: A working installation made of four linked parts: a compost-heated incubator growing mouse muscle cells as lab-grown meat, an alkaline hydrolysis unit that turns tissue and slaughterhouse refuse into fertiliser, hydroponic beds growing plants without soil, and a control room collecting sensor data from the other parts. It was first staged as a three-week durational experiment at PS Art Space, Fremantle, in February 2022, with public workshops, a symposium, dinner events, live streaming and a documentary. It received an Award of Distinction in Artificial Intelligence & Life Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2023.

title: A Tale of Two Seeds: Sound and Silence in Latin America's Andean Plain
summary: A sound installation built from field recordings of soils and plants in Colombia's Eastern Plains, recorded above and below ground, together with recordings of the electrical conductivity of soy and amaranth plants, which are sonified. FACT describes the recordings as contrasting soy monocultures with soy-amaranth polycultures, where amaranth grows despite herbicide use. Accompanying video works (On Vegetal Politics, Botánica Transgénica) and a blockchain application address the stock-market valuation and patenting of genetically modified plants; the work received the 2023 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica in Digital Musics & Sound Art.

title: Absence
summary: Absence is a 3D-animated short film (10 min per the artist, 12 min per the producer Autour de Minuit), in French with English subtitles. An old homeless man collapses alone in a square; passers-by avoid, ignore or help him, until journalists take an interest and he becomes the centre of an escalating media event. It received an Award of Distinction in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: African Space Makers
summary: A 50-minute interactive 360-degree VR experience made in Nairobi, shown in Venice VR Expanded 2020. The viewer chooses a gender and the order in which to visit five creative spaces run by Nairobi collectives, and in each space chooses what to do and where to go next.

title: AI and the Art of Historical Reinterpretation – Filling Gender Bias Gaps
summary: An ongoing project that uses AI image generation to build a growing fictional archive of 'historical images' in which male figures in known historical photographs are replaced by female or nonbinary figures; the collection is spread across digital platforms so it can be scraped as training data for future AI models. In the exhibition installation, a selection of images related to technology is shown with a slide projector on a vintage projection screen.

title: AI War Cloud Database
media: Network / data | Online / net art | AI / generative
summary: AI War Cloud Database is an online interactive database and visualisation (aiwar.cloud) that catalogues AI systems used to make automated decisions in warfare and maps where the same types of tools appear in commercial products such as iris scanners, chatbots, robot vacuums and mapping tools, along with the companies and governments involved. Users explore the material through network graphs, a searchable table and interactive stories; the project describes itself as both an interactive database and a tangible interactive installation. It received the S+T+ARTS Prize 2025 Grand Prize – Artistic Exploration and was shown in the S+T+ARTS Prize exhibition at Ars Electronica Festival 2025 in Linz.

title: Anthem
summary: Anthem is an installation of four suspended devices modelled on tree tumours (burls), 3D-printed and fitted with speakers, microphones and sound processors. It responds in real time to visitors' vocalisations with machine-generated animal-like calls. It was first shown at the centre of Santillán's exhibition ¿Qué se siente ser tierra? at the Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito (2025–2026) and again at the 2026 Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale.

title: Anxious Body
summary: Anxious Body is a 5'47 2D digital animated short without dialogue, commissioned by Towada Art Center and produced by Miyu Productions and New Deer (2021), with sound by Yuka C. Honda. It shows fingers, cellophane tape and a dispenser, a mechanical pencil, tennis racket strings, a sponge and a snake-like creature touching, pulling and pressing against one another. It received an Award of Distinction in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Ausente
media: Camera / computer vision | AI / generative | Projection
summary: An interactive installation (Dyscrimina / Ausente) presented at the 44th International Symposium of Contemporary Art of Baie-Saint-Paul: a surveillance-style projection shows visitors in real time, and people are erased from the frame. Across four stations using AI and computer vision, the public collectively teaches the machine which characteristics to recognize; those outside the resulting vocabulary are designated « non-choisi.e » and progressively removed from the image.

title: Avatar Robot Cafe DAWN ver.β
summary: Avatar Robot Cafe DAWN ver.β is a permanent café in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, run by Ory Lab, where people who have difficulty going out because of illness, disability, caregiving or distance work as “pilots”, remotely operating the avatar robots OriHime and OriHime-D from home or hospital through the robots' cameras, microphones and speakers, in some cases by eye-gaze input. Visitors are seated, order, are served drinks and talk with the pilots through the robots; the project also matches pilots with employers through Ory Lab's Avatar Guild staffing agency. It received the Golden Nica in Digital Communities at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Awakening
summary: A projection mapping work shown on the facade of CHIJMES at the Singapore Night Festival 2025 (22 Aug-6 Sep), made by Tororo.aoi (Asher Yeo) as part of the festival's third Projection Mapping Masterclass, led by the Malaysian collective Filamen. According to the festival, it takes Singapore's island and port history as its subject, starting from a metaphorical dive into a shipwreck.

title: Azibuye – The Occupation
summary: Azibuye – The Occupation is a 360-degree virtual reality documentary following Masello Motana, a performance artist, and Evan Abrahamse, an activist and former Umkhonto we Sizwe member, who occupy a mansion in an affluent part of Johannesburg that has stood empty and decaying for about 20 years, as an act about land ownership. The viewer is placed inside the house with them; the film includes a recorded phone interview with the house's owner. Produced by Electric South, it premiered in the New Frontier section of the Sundance Film Festival in 2020.

title: Añoranzas (Yira Yira)
summary: Añoranzas (Yira Yira) is an installation with 16mm colour film made by recycling celluloid combs, screened with a 16mm film projector. It refers to Argentine film pioneer Federico Valle, whose surviving films, after a 1926 fire, were sold to a comb factory that used the celluloid as raw material. The work was realised with a 2023 CIFO-Ars Electronica Award and shown at the LENTOS Kunstmuseum during Ars Electronica Festival 2023.

title: Baitul Ma'mur: House of Angels
summary: A bio-art project by Sarah Khan and Joe Davis that encodes the Arabic phrase "Subhan Allah" multiple times into synthesized DNA molecules, using a coding scheme modelled on the repeating geometries of Islamic art; according to the artists, a 1mm layer of this DNA on the head of a straight pin holds 2.417 quintillion repetitions ("angels"). The work is presented with a glass and aluminum "Baitul Ma'mur" structure with electronics, project graphics and a short documentary film. It received an Honorary Mention in the Prix Ars Electronica 2021, Artificial Intelligence & Life Art category.

title: Behind Shirley
media: Screen / monitor | VR / AR / XR | Material / sculpture
summary: An installation made in 2020 consisting of a video-essay, two 3D-printed busts and an augmented reality application. It addresses the 'Shirley cards' used to calibrate skin tones in colour photography and the failure of current facial recognition software to register darker skin. It was shown at the 5th Istanbul Design Biennial (2020) and in the exhibition Digital Shadows at OBA Oosterdok, Amsterdam (until 26 Feb 2023), and received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Bemol
summary: An installation of video, photography and sound composition shown at Centro Cultural Recoleta for the 17th Bienal de Artes Mediales de Santiago (2025). It is built from audio recordings, photographs and video the artist made of her home and its surroundings in Santiago's Barrio Yungay after resettling there in 2024, assembled as what she calls an 'anti-archive'; two sound-visual concerts accompanied it.

title: Broken Spectre
summary: Broken Spectre (2022) is a feature-length immersive video installation (about 70–74 minutes) on deforestation and environmental crime along the Trans-Amazonian Highway in the Brazilian Amazon, made with cinematographer Trevor Tweeten and composer Ben Frost. It alternates footage from an aerial multispectral camera flown from a helicopter, ultraviolet macro time-lapse of the forest floor, and black-and-white infrared 35mm film of ranchers, gold miners and Indigenous communities, including a speech to camera by Yanomami woman Adneia. Visitors watch it in a gallery with a spatialised soundtrack; it received the 2023 S+T+ARTS Grand Prize – Innovative Collaboration.

title: Build Up the House II
summary: Build Up the House II is an animated video shown on more than 92 electronic billboards in Times Square nightly from 11:57pm to midnight throughout March 2025 as part of Midnight Moment, presented with ART on THE MART. Silhouettes of dancers leap, spin and vogue across colored patterns that reference the artist's East African heritage and textiles, as an homage to house music and its queer and POC roots. It follows Build Up the House, a 2024 projection on the facade of THE MART in Chicago marking the 40th anniversary of house music; a public DJ dance party accompanied the Times Square presentation on 14 March 2025.

title: Café Kuba
summary: A cinematic installation (film, about 27 minutes, in French and Lingala, with 3D sound) built around a mobile street coffee cart in Kinshasa that Shongo converted into a recording device. Filmed after the M23 capture of Goma and Bukavu in early 2025, it follows the cart and a coffee vendor through the city's streets and conversations, with fictional elements such as masked figures holding electronic waste and licence plates; it won the State of the ART(ist) prize at Ars Electronica 2025.

title: Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Power and Technology, 1500-2025
summary: A diagram more than 24 metres long and 3 metres high, made as a diptych of hundreds of hand-drawn illustrations and short texts, that maps communication, computation, classification and control from 1500 to the present. Time runs vertically and systems run horizontally, so visitors can follow a theme, a period or a set of ideas. Two handmade books are shown with it, and visitors are invited to annotate them in pencil.

title: Cangjie's Poetry
media: AI / generative | Camera / computer vision | Projection
summary: An installation in which an AI system named Cangjie, a neural network trained on the constructions of over 9,000 Chinese characters, watches its surroundings through a camera and turns the live feed into new symbols built from Chinese strokes, shown as a moving pixelated landscape on a first projection. A second projection shows descriptive sentences the system generates about the scene, rendered as flowing ink 'poetry' assembled with fragments of the captured imagery. Visitors meet both projections changing in real time with what the camera sees.

title: catástrofe orquestra #1 (Ato I)
summary: An installation made for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo (2025): 11 suspended panels of recycled matchbox fragments on thin wooden slats, among which 64 motor-driven rope pendulums carrying pieces of coal strike leather drums. The coal shatters on impact; the sounds are picked up by microphones and amplified into a soundscape with noises and voices, and the debris accumulates on the floor. The work later travelled with the Bienal's itinerant exhibitions, including to the Pinacoteca do Ceará and the Centro Cultural La Moneda in Santiago.

title: CENTO
media: VR / AR / XR | Online / net art | Screen / monitor
summary: CENTO is an augmented-reality creature, geolocated above the eighth-floor terrace of the Whitney Museum of American Art, together with a video that tours the creature's imagined habitat (nest, refueling chamber, and the space where it metabolizes fuel and takes flight). Using the free 4th Wall app, on site or from anywhere, viewers choose one of twelve feathers, each with a function such as communication, navigation or energy conversion, and add it to the creature's body, which is updated over time. It is a Whitney artport commission; the title refers to a poem made of lines taken from other poets' works.

title: CHIMERIA
media: Performance / body | VR / AR / XR | Camera / computer vision
summary: CHIMERIA is a project, performance and installation in which head-mounted displays move a participant's vision to other parts of the body, such as the toes, so that the feet act as the head. Volunteers recruited through a publicly circulated phone number lived together in a Tokyo residence, adapting to an environment built for upright bodies with tube-fed liquid food, wire-driven prosthetics and a toilet used kneeling. Outsiders could visit the space, but only by imitating the environment and becoming part of it.

title: Chosho Hakkei in Rittor Base - HPL ver
summary: A five-track, roughly 42-minute 3D audio album for headphone listening, made with the HPL binaural process developed with engineer Jiro Kubo (ACOUSTIC FIELD). It reconstructs evala's 2019 sound installations 'Chosho Hakkei' in the Nakazu Banshou-en daimyo garden in Marugame, Kagawa, placed on a bridge, on a small island and in the oldest extant tea house there, first restaged as a 3D sound piece at Rittor Base. Listeners follow, on headphones, a route through the garden's recorded and composed sounds.

title: Chotlung: traversing spirits, redemptive songs
summary: A single-channel video (8:50 minutes) shown with a textile installation of pieces handwoven by the artist, co-commissioned by Colomboscope and Ghost 2568 and exhibited at Colomboscope: Rhythm Alliances in Colombo. The video shows looms and Yakthung rituals at Mukkumlung sacred mountain and the Imbiri Yangthangwa (Tamor river) region of eastern Nepal, alongside protests against hydropower dams and a proposed cable car; the textiles have also been carried in demonstrations.

title: Chuly? Chuly
summary: An XR video game and live motion-capture performance (Ukrainian title Чули? Чули, 'Have you heard? We've heard' / 'Have you felt it? We've felt it'), first developed as a demo in Deep Space 8K at the Ars Electronica Center. In the first act a player crosses a game world guided by an AI-processed narration of a woman's story of seeing giants; in the second a dancer in an inertial motion-capture suit, whose calibration drifts, enters, and player and dancer exchange suit parts and controller, so the player becomes a non-player character and the dancer controls the camera. It received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2024.

title: Circles of Rhythm and Rains
summary: Circles of Rhythm and Rains (also given as Circle of Rhythms / Circle of Rhythms & Rains) is a kinetic sound installation shown at the Rio Complex for Colomboscope 2026, co-commissioned with 421 Arts Campus. Traditional Tamil drums used in Koothu (thavil, mathalam, udukkai, parai, mirudhangam), handcrafted with artisan Vadivel Aananthashankar from reclaimed wood and repurposed materials, are arranged in a circle and struck by automated tappers driven by Arduino and motors, built with DreamSpace Academy/lab. Visitors meet programmed, pulsating beat cycles played without a human drummer.

title: Codex Virtualis_Genesis
summary: An AI-art-science project that generates an open-ended taxonomic collection of speculative life forms by training generative networks on microscopy footage of bacteria and archaea combined with cellular-automata models. The installation, distributed across three projections, shows the process from the simplest organisms through 'virtual genesis' to a final rendering with an AI-generated taxonomic name. It was made during the SETI x AI residency (SETI Institute and Ars Electronica Futurelab, European ARTificial Intelligence Lab) in 2021 and received an Honorary Mention at Prix Ars Electronica 2023.

title: Coin Laundry
summary: Coin Laundry is an installation by the pseudonymous artist XCOPY, presented on the Nguyen Wahed stand in the Zero 10 section of Art Basel Miami Beach in December 2025 and staged as a laundromat. According to the gallery, participants enter an ephemeral network through fungible tokens inscribed in code, in a collective performance planned to last a decade; the work was presented in partnership with Shape.

title: Collective Body
media: VR / AR / XR | Performance / body | Sound
summary: Collective Body is a 19-minute multi-user virtual reality dance experience set in a New Mexican storm, in which participants are guided through stages: beginning alone, discovering the unfamiliar, first encounters and moving together. An algorithmic system analyses each participant's movement and assigns one of sixteen avatars, each represented as a natural element with its own musical theme; participants then meet one other person and finally the whole group. It runs on Meta Quest 3 headsets with almost full-body tracking and no other wearables; it was shown at Venice Immersive 2025 and at Lincoln Center.

title: Compose
summary: Yuko Mohri's exhibition for the Japan Pavilion at the 60th Venice Biennale (20 April to 24 November 2024), curated by Sook-Kyung Lee, made of two site-specific installations built mostly from materials found locally. In Moré Moré (Leaky), the artist creates water leaks in the pavilion and catches them with household goods, with pumps circulating the water through a large kinetic sculpture; rain can enter through the open ceiling. In Decomposition, electrodes in local fruit turn their changing moisture into signals that modulate drone sounds and lights as the fruit ripens and decays, after which it goes to compost.

title: Convergence
summary: Convergence is a 35-minute piece for string ensemble and AI system, made with Ensemble Resonanz, that exists as a staged version (premiered in Bonn, October 2020; revised in Dresden, 2023) and a digital-only streamed version (premiered February 2021, commissioned by Eclat Festival). Deep-learning models (auto-encoders and GANs, with audio programming by IRCAM researchers) learn features of the musicians' faces, bodies and voices, and the performers, guided by a computer voice, interact with the generated counterparts of themselves. It won the 2021 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art.

title: Conversations Beyond the Ordinary
summary: Conversations Beyond the Ordinary is an ensemble of three interactive installations (a coffee vending machine, a photocopier and a microwave) fitted with sensors, custom software and generative AI so that they converse with visitors. Visitors have to persuade the coffee machine to brew them a coffee, draw doodles that the photocopier turns into rendered prints they can take home, and use the microwave to give a voice to objects placed inside it. It received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art+ at Prix Ars Electronica 2024 and was shown at the Ars Electronica Festival 2024; the coffee machine and microwave were developed during a residency at iii (instrument inventors initiative).

title: Dari Pulau Ke Pulau (From One Island to Another)
summary: A projection mapping work shown on the facade of CHIJMES at the Singapore Night Festival 2025 (22 Aug-6 Sep), made by HAFI (Hafizah Jainal) as part of the festival's third Projection Mapping Masterclass, led by the Malaysian collective Filamen. Using illustration and moving images, it traces the routes of the artist's maternal and paternal grandparents from Alor Gajah, Melaka, and Pacitan, East Java, to Singapore.

title: Different Shades of Water
summary: A series of five digital paintings made in Microsoft Word and issued as NFTs, restaging David Hockney's Portrait of an Artist (Pool with Two Figures) (1972) with a Black man as the poolside bather under different daylight and water colours. The works were shown at 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair at Somerset House, London, in October 2021 and auctioned online by Christie's, the first NFT by a contemporary African artist offered by Christie's in Europe.

title: Dobra do tempo infinito (Fold of Infinite Time)
artist: Glicéria Tupinambá, Atã Tupinambá Group & Tupinambá Community of Serra do Padeiro
summary: Dobra do tempo infinito is a video installation shown in the Hãhãwpuá Pavilion (Brazil) at the 60th Venice Biennale, combining video with seeds, leaves, soil, fishing nets, jereré and samburá. The video records workshops Glicéria Tupinambá organised in the communities of Serra do Padeiro and Olivença (Bahia), in which masters made canoes, fishing nets and net-weaving needles and went fishing with trawls and tarrafas; the footage was shot by young people of the Atã Tupinambá Group with Augusto Santos (Method_av). The venue text links the stitches of fishing nets to the weaving of traditional Tupinambá clothing.

title: Double Poser
summary: Double Poser is a 38-minute auto-played game made with the Unity game engine (4k, colour, stereo sound), commissioned by the Hayward Gallery, London, and Art Sonje Center, Seoul, and shown in the Hayward's HENI Project Space from 1 December 2023 to 7 January 2024. Reinterpreting components of Kim's Cutter III (2023), it takes the Hayward's brutalist architecture as a starting point and combines computer-generated imagery, video game aesthetics and skateboarding culture. Visitors watch it as a video in the gallery.

title: Dreams Have No Titles
summary: Sedira's installation for the French Pavilion at the 59th Venice Biennale (2022): a series of interlocking film sets, including a re-creation of her London living room, a shelf of film reels referencing the Cinémathèque Algérienne, a ballroom bar and a cinema room, combined with a film of re-enactments and 'makings of' scenes. It draws on Algerian, French and Italian militant cinema of the 1960s and 1970s, including The Battle of Algiers and the rediscovered Les Mains libres. Visitors walk through the sets, watch the film and at times meet two performers dancing the tango.

title: Drifting Bodies
summary: A four-channel video installation (colour, sound, 10 min 30 sec, with curtains and mattress) that pairs a silent projection of the Jewel Rain Vortex indoor waterfall at Singapore's Changi Airport with three channels of footage and spatialised sound from Thailand's Vajiralongkorn Dam Reservoir, where displaced Karen families live on floating rafts; the two sites are linked by a shared hydroelectric power grid. Visitors walk through the waterfall projection screens to reach the reservoir footage. It was first shown at Storefront for Art and Architecture, New York (2025), and at Singapore Biennale 2025 alongside the sound work The Humming of the Power Grid and a fundraising Water Campaign for the reservoir community.

title: EMPEROR
summary: EMPEROR is a 40-minute single-user interactive VR narrative, produced by Atlas V with Reynard Films and France Télévisions, set inside the mind of a father with aphasia, drawn as a hand-drawn monochrome landscape. The user takes the father's point of view alongside his daughter, using hand tracking to pick up objects, write letters and handle word cards in speech-therapy scenes, some of which are designed to fail at first. It is based on the story of co-director Marion Burger's father.

title: Endangered Gestures
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Text / print
summary: A short film (4K single-channel video, 6'10'') and artist book (Small Book of Endangered Gestures) showing hand gestures generated with AI imaging for words and phrases that began disappearing from U.S. government websites, documents and archives in March 2025. Each censored word is paired with a proposed gesture made by hands that are almost but not quite human. It received a Prix Ars Electronica Honorary Mention (New Animation Art) and was shortlisted for the LUMA Rencontres Dummy Book Award in 2026.

title: Estate (July 10, 2022)
media: AI / generative | Camera / computer vision | Material / sculpture
summary: Estate (July 10, 2022) is a sculpture in the form of a door intercom mounted on a folding screen, shown at the Whitney Biennial 2026. A camera in the work monitors its surroundings, and an AI model trained on the social media posts of a deceased person from a creative field speaks in a cloned voice when visitors come near, responding with fragments of recollection (for example a recipe when someone passes holding a drink). An LED screen counts the years, days, hours and minutes since that person's death.

title: Evaporating Symphony
summary: An installation of 3D-printed metal stones on elevated stainless steel panels at varying heights, heated through heat conductors, thermal sensors, relays and a thermal controller, with roller pumps and water pipes delivering droplets of water. Each droplet that touches a stone evaporates in under a second with a soft percussive sound, which is amplified in the space. It was shown at the 13th Seoul Mediacity Biennale, Séance: Technology of the Spirit, Seoul Museum of Art (2025).

title: Eyes of Shame (Gėdos akys)
summary: Eyes of Shame is a 40-minute animated virtual reality film (Lithuania, France, Croatia). It follows 14-year-old Eyeless in a hospital for troubled teenagers: when a nurse forces her to eat, unfinished memories begin to interrupt the present, and the viewer is placed in her point of view. It premiered in the Venice Immersive competition in 2026 and draws on the director's volunteering at a hospital for teenagers in Vilnius, where he has run animation workshops since 2014.

title: F*ckai? (Famous)
summary: F*ckai? (Famous) is a five-minute 3D-animated short film by Toronto director and animator Jordan Clarke. Its story, about an AI that wanted to be famous, was generated by OpenAI in response to his prompt and voiced by an AI, then paraphrased and edited by Clarke, who animated, composited, sound-designed and edited the film himself. It closes his 'f*ckai?' series of short films and received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at the 2024 Prix Ars Electronica.

title: Fashion Show for Elders
summary: Fashion Show for Elders is a series of AI-generated images by Nigerian filmmaker Malik Afegbua showing elderly African models on a runway in outfits mixing traditional Nigerian dress with futuristic designs. The show never took place: the models and clothes were produced with several AI image generators, and the images were shared online, where many viewers took them for a real event.

title: FEARDEATHLOVEDEATH
summary: A 17-minute film shot on Super 16mm and transferred to Full HD, commissioned by Röda Sten Konsthall, Gothenburg. It is divided into chapters: the contents of a recently deceased man's bedroom described in an invented one-word language, an abstract time-based painting sequence, a love poem, and an alligator appearing in the clouds. Viewers watch it as a single-channel film in screenings and exhibitions.

title: Foragers
summary: A film of about an hour combining documentary, scripted fiction and archival footage, shot mainly in the Galilee, the Golan Heights and around Jerusalem. It follows Palestinian foragers gathering za'atar and 'akkoub, plants whose wild harvesting is restricted under Israeli nature-protection law, and stages court hearings co-scripted with lawyer Rabea Eghbariah. Viewers watch it as a film in cinemas, festivals and exhibitions.

title: From Hand to Mouth
summary: An installation of steel, glass, a workshop crane, tubes and a pump in which a glass fermenter holds a replica of the right hand of Michelangelo's David, 3D-printed in the bioplastic PHB. PHB-producing bacteria (including Cupriavidus necator) in the fermenter gradually metabolise the hand and alter its form. It belongs to chapter 5 of Feuerstein's METABOLICA project and was shown in Renaissance 3.0 at ZKM Karlsruhe (2023), whose collection holds it.

title: From Noise
media: AI / generative | Network / data | Text / print
summary: From Noise is a series of 12 NFTs from one algorithm by Tyler Hobbs that translates the spontaneous gestural marks of painters such as Cy Twombly and Joan Mitchell into code; each work contains more than 4,000 marks. At Zero 10, Art Basel Miami Beach 2025 (SOLOS stand), it was shown as four large-format prints on wood varnished by the artist, with boxed sets of screen prints, Translated Gestures, taken from details of the outputs.

title: fugue notes
summary: fugue notes is a film (HD digital video and 16mm, with sound) in which the artist's original plan for a film is replaced by its notes: in deep shadow and darkness, a voiceover links eroding autobiographical memory with the failed image. It was commissioned by CIRCUIT for Leap to the Place of Two Pools at Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery, Wellington (2025), and was later screened at Artspace Aotearoa in 2026 with the artist reading the script live.

title: FuneralPlay
summary: A website presented as a fictitious online funeral platform where mourners attend simulated funerals for lost loved ones in themed virtual mausoleums, such as a mahjong room, a gallery of cat memes or a feng shui master's orchard. Users can choose to delete a deceased person's digital footprint, keep it as an inheritance, or donate it to a collective Memorial Hall, and can give NFTs as memorial gifts; exploring a scene reveals hidden clues and rewards. The platform states it has no actual financial function and does not share data with other platforms.

title: Garden of the Broken Hearted
summary: An installation in the Arsenale at the 61st Venice Biennale (In Minor Keys): a large olive tree placed on a rotating stage, onto which a video is projected. The projected footage shows the same tree, filmed before its transport to Venice.

title: GR-AI-N
media: Robotics / kinetics | Camera / computer vision | Material / sculpture
summary: GR-AI-N is a digital-craft workflow that uses discarded offcuts from the wood industry: pieces are scanned, AI-powered tools extract their grain patterns, texture and imperfections, and robotic assembly and milling build objects (mirrors, a headboard) as 3D mosaics of irregular pieces that keep the grain continuous. It was developed in the VOJEXT S+T+ARTS residency 'Robotics in Arts and Crafts' in Barcelona and was nominated for the 2024 S+T+ARTS Prize.

title: Guanaquerx
summary: Guanaquerx is a four-legged robot modelled on the guanaco, partly made from caña colihue bamboo and dressed in Andean textiles. In January 2024, about 30 people with 58 mules and horses took it across the Andes from Argentina to the Chilean border over seven days, re-enacting the 1817 crossing by San Martín's army; mules carried the robot where the ground was too rough for it. The robot records sound and images, emits a synthetic whinny, beats a drum, waves a flag and carries a plaque with 'Pluriversal Laws of Robotics'. The work won the 2025 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica and was shown at the Ars Electronica Festival 2025.

title: HANDMADE
summary: HANDMADE is a video diptych of about 11 minutes, originally conceived for two 4K monitors and presented at MoMA from November 2023 in the ground-floor Gund Lobby on a large media wall. One part shows digitally manipulated footage of a gale-force storm on Lake Huron, filmed by Thornton with a handheld camera while lying down; the other shows a physicist at Caltech making a handwoven sensing device for a research project on antimatter. These are interspersed with film recordings of fluid-dynamics studies that Thornton found during her 2019 residency in the Caltech-Huntington Program in Visual Culture.

title: Harvesting Climate Action
media: Material / sculpture | Network / data | Online / net art
summary: Harvesting Climate Action was a six-week installation in Hackney Service Centre, London (autumn 2025), part of Ling Tan's Low Carbon Chinatown project, made with Hackney Council's Climate Team. Its centre was 100 recyclable cardboard stools, each printed on one side with a 'Climate Action' (from individual to borough-wide) and on the other with the carbon footprint of a meal ingredient, alongside data maps, food-making videos, audio stories and living produce. The installation then became a 'Low Carbon Banquet for a Hundred', where 100 members of the public each took a stool, sat with strangers over low carbon East and Southeast Asian dishes, debated and voted on the actions, and took their stool home; the 100 Climate Actions also exist as an online toolkit. It received an Honorary Mention (Digital Humanity) at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Hinat
summary: A multi-panel installation made during an AlUla residency in 2022, named after Hinat, a Nabataean woman whose tomb (Tomb 117) is at Hegra. Painted and photo-transferred collages of AlUla landscapes have rectangles cut out, into which videos are projected; the videos, generated with machine learning from footage of three women from AlUla wearing coloured fabrics, show ghostly figures moving across the landscapes. It was shown in 'Art of the Kingdom' at the Saudi Arabian Museum of Contemporary Art.

title: Holly+
media: Sound | AI / machine learning | Network / data
summary: A public website where anyone can upload audio and get it back 'sung' in a machine-learning model of Holly Herndon's voice, built with Never Before Heard Sounds. What people make is theirs to use; 'official' Holly+ works are voted on by a DAO of stewards, sold as NFTs, with profits split between the maker, the DAO treasury and Herndon.

title: Homo Machina (Human Machine, a.k.a. Gay Machine)
media: Material / sculpture | Screen / monitor | Camera / computer vision
summary: A life-size sculptural digital console shown at the Whitney Biennial 2026. It combines sculpture with video and surveillance footage and functions as a self-portrait. The neon-green surface carries a cast face and 3D-printed parts, and at its centre a clear womb holds a motor-driven ouroboros.

title: Honorata
summary: Honorata is a 15-minute multichannel song conceived as a lullaby, commissioned by MUAC for its Espacio de Experimentación Sonora in Mexico City, where it was shown from 11 October 2025 to April 2026. Visitors listen to Nasta's voice with bass, viola, guitar, Rhodes piano, Hammond organ and synthesisers, spatialised across the room's 22 channels by Tobías Álvarez. The piece was composed during Nasta's pregnancy and finished a few months after the birth.

title: Hotel Infinity
summary: Hotel Infinity is a room-scale VR puzzle game by Studio Chyr, set in a hotel built from non-Euclidean, looping architecture. Players move through hallways and ballrooms by physically walking inside a play area of about 2 x 2 metres, with portals folding the space, and solve puzzles to uncover the hotel's secrets. It was released for Meta Quest and PS VR2 on 13 November 2025 and selected for Venice Immersive 2026.

title: huě iànn
artist: Yu-Han Chen, Ching-Wen Hsu, Ruei-Sin Jhang, Li-Hua Zhan, Tung-En Chien, Pei-Chi Wu
summary: huě iànn is a VR animated video made by a six-person team from the Department of Visual Communication Design at Jinwen University of Science and Technology, Taiwan. It addresses events in Taiwan's history connected to freedom of speech, starting from the Taiyuan incident. It received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2023.

title: I DIDNT REALISE YOU THOUGHT LIKE THAT
summary: An online game for web and mobile, released by Serpentine on 21 May 2026, in which players decide whether to open a door to fictional characters, conspiracy agents or 'Influencers' who ask to enter on the basis of their stated beliefs. The game simulates a real-time feed, and players meet a cast of characters and reach different endings depending on their choices. It is described as the next chapter of THE DELUSION, the multiplayer game exhibition at Serpentine North (September 2025 to January 2026), where a gallery version with a transparent door and a screen was the first work visitors encountered.

title: I'm Feeling Lucky
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: A real-time generative installation of infinite runtime in which a historically and geographically ambiguous 3D landscape, generated with game engine technology, is populated with thousands of figures taken from Google Street View and turned into 3D models by a deep neural network. A virtual camera pans endlessly across the landscape, a format the artist relates to 19th-century panorama paintings; a 360° fulldome version (Panorama: I'm Feeling Lucky) was shown at the SAT in Montréal. Sound design and composition by Tatum Wilson.

title: I.AM.ISIGO Digital Mystery System
media: Online / net art | Network / data | Material / sculpture
summary: A digital tool by Bubu Ogisi's label I.AM.ISIGO that archives knowledge of African weaving techniques gathered through research with artisan communities, and lets users create new weaving patterns. It was shown in the S+T+ARTS exhibition at Ars Electronica Festival 2024 in the context of the STARTS4Africa project.

title: If You Have Starry Skies in Your Eyes
summary: A prosthetic eye designed, made and worn by the artist, who lost the sight of her right eye as a child; it contains a magnetic sensor, an LED and a battery encapsulated in medical-grade acrylic resin, and lights up when a magnet is brought near. The project, presented with a video, follows an earlier starry-sky-patterned prosthetic eye she wears daily, and received an Award of Distinction in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2024.

title: IGÚN
summary: An ongoing series of StyleGAN models trained on images of Benin Bronzes looted from the Benin Kingdom during the 1897 British invasion, now held in museum collections. It generates synthetic prototypes of objects that might have been cast during the 17-year interregnum (1897–1914), when no Oba commissioned work; datasets were extended with ceremonial heads in wood and pottery because there were too few bronze images to train the model. The Lumen Prize presentation shows video of latent-space interpolations; the work won the Lumen Prize Global South Award in 2021.

title: In 36,000 Ways (Site-Specific Installation)
summary: In 36,000 Ways (Site-Specific Installation) is a single-visitor booth in which the visitor is shown a piece of missile shrapnel the artist collected on front lines in Ukraine. The visitor's presence and physiological signals, including heartbeat, are picked up without contact and shape a low-frequency soundscape. The title refers to the roughly 36,000 fragments a fragmentation weapon breaks into; the booth is a variation of an ongoing project, shown in the IDFA DocLab Competition 2025, with a larger walk-through version in development.

title: In a Small Room
media: AI / generative | VR / AR / XR | Screen / monitor
summary: A project titled in full 'In a Small Room: The Gap between Advertising and Reality', made as a Royal College of Art (Information Experience Design) degree project, about cramped housing in London and Seoul and the advertising images used to rent it. It has four parts: an interactive web application (CycleGAN) into which visitors put a photo of a real room and receive an advertising-style image, a VR installation of an 'advertising' room entered from a bed in a built room, two films shot in the same Seoul goshiwon room (a documentary and an advertisement), and a research dissertation. It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Humanity at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: Island Waters
summary: A 60-second animated video projection-mapped onto the facade of CHIJMES at the Singapore Night Festival 2025 (22 Aug-6 Sep), commissioned by the National Heritage Board and made by illustrator and motion designer Lim KangLi in the festival's Projection Mapping Masterclass. The animation moves from a ripple down to the seabed, up through maritime routes and back to the surface, with colours drawn from Peranakan porcelain.

title: khalil
summary: khalil is a site-specific multimedia installation by Khaled Sabsabi in In Minor Keys, the main exhibition of the 61st Venice Biennale (2026), made of object, video, scent and sound. Its title is the Arabic word for close friend or companion. Sabsabi showed it at the same time as conference of one's self in the Australia Pavilion, and he describes the two as complementary works.

title: Kissing of the Threshold
summary: Kissing of the Threshold (Urdu: آستان بوس) is a project by Fazal Rizvi centred on Shia traditions of mourning and remembrance, shown as a new commission at Sharjah Biennial 16 (2025). Dawn's review describes a large-scale installation with buckets of water, a mound representing a grave, and an eight-channel audio work in which the artist's voice recites soz; the Sharjah Art Foundation also published it as a two-part artist book of calligraphy and performative photographs referring to the Ghusaals in Pakistan, who wash and prepare the bodies of the dead.

title: Knit II
summary: Knit II (2021) is a 4K video by Kawita Vatanajyankur, listed on the Simon Lee Foundation Institute of Contemporary Asian Art (AGWA) artist page. It belongs to her knitting works within the Performing Textiles series, in which the artist uses her own body as the mechanism of a knitting machine, weaving red yarn into a web-like fabric on camera. Viewers watch the recorded performance as a video.

title: kus
summary: kus (2025) is an installation with audio shown at the Aichi Arts Center (8F) in Aichi Triennale 2025, made by travelling between Mayunkiki's hometown of Asahikawa, Hokkaido, and the Tenryu River basin. Her team recorded sounds of present-day railways and the natural environment and overlapped them with recordings of traditional Ainu song. The work draws on the history of her grandfather Kawamura Kaneto, an Ainu leader and surveying engineer who supervised railway construction between Tenryukyo and Mikawa-Kawai, and was presented together with her performance work kuste.

title: L'Onde du Midi
summary: L'Onde du Midi is a permanent kinetic sculpture commissioned by the Musée du Louvre and inaugurated in January 2020 above the Escalier du Midi (Sully wing). It consists of 128 aluminium tubes suspended from nearly invisible cables driven by motors; computer-programmed sequences move the roughly 10-metre horizontal plane in slow undulations between 3 and 4.5 metres high. Visitors on the staircase watch the shifting configurations.

title: La laguna parla
summary: La laguna parla is a 35-minute collective, smartphone-guided ritual about the Venice lagoon, water and collective power, made for the tenth anniversary of Venice Immersive (2026), in which hundreds of participants take part with their own phones. It is an adaptation of The Waterbodies Orchestra, an earlier work by The Confluence of European Water Bodies and The Smartphone Orchestra made to give a voice to European water bodies. In Smartphone Orchestra experiences, participants receive instructions, prompts, questions and games on their phones that lead them to interact with the other people in the room.

title: Laundry Nocturne
summary: Laundry Nocturne (2026) is a multi-channel video projection with field recordings, shown in Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice, the Hong Kong collateral exhibition of the 61st Venice Biennale curated by the Hong Kong Museum of Art. Silhouettes of laundry hung between buildings are projected in the room in a way that simulates moonlight entering through the space's windows. A soundtrack of night-time recordings from Hong Kong, including a wastewater treatment plant, a newspaper-printing facility and a postal sorting centre, plays from a radio in the room.

title: Le Miroir
summary: Le Miroir is an experimental film produced at Le Fresnoy – Studio national des arts contemporains, in which the artist interacts with her own virtual double, a MetaHuman generated from her appearance, in mental landscapes structured around figures inspired by psychoanalytic archetypes (Ego, Superego, Id, Self). It combines real-time 3D animation, motion capture, photogrammetry, miniature sets and filmed sequences, with a soundtrack of synthesizers and electroacoustic composition. It was shown in Le Fresnoy's Panorama 27 and received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Light Keeper
summary: A GPS-enabled sound walk and light installation commissioned for Singapore Biennale 2025 at Fort Canning Park. Visitors use a GPS-enabled app that guides them to five sites in the park, where audio vignettes based on the artists' encounters with lighthouses, lighthouse keepers and crypto-linguists play; at the Fort Canning Lighthouse, a programmed, looped light cycle runs after dusk. A companion three-channel video, Light Keeper: Signal (2025, 7 min 58 sec), is shown at Fort Canning Centre.

title: Liquid Crystal
summary: A Whitney artport commission of seven short videos, one for each day of the week, shown on whitney.org at sunrise and sunset in New York (Apr–Jul 2023). Each video opens on a natural surface (leaves and moss, sand, gravel, snow, broken ice) that the artist's hands push aside to reveal a screen of synthesized video patterns.

title: Makȟóčhe Kiŋ Oíč'iwa (The Land Paints Itself)
summary: A digital video with sound commissioned by CIRCUIT Artist Moving Image and shown in the group exhibition Leap to the Place of Two Pools at Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery, Wellington (1 February – 6 April 2025). According to the gallery, the work pairs technologies of dreaming and AI to imagine Indigenous futures patterned across unceded land, marked by stones whose own language emerges as a conduit to multivocal storytelling.

title: Mapping Uncertain Landscape: The Satellite
media: Robotics / kinetics | Network / data | Text / print
summary: An installation in which a plotter machine built by the artist continuously draws maps of Ukrainian terrain on a large roll of paper, translating vegetation-index data (NDRE/NDVI) from the commercial crop-monitoring satellite EOS SAT into colours. The first version focuses on a road between Ivankiv and the Belarus border; later map series, made with ecologists and earth scientists, follow vegetation changes around the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam (6 June 2023) and the first Russian offensive on Kyiv. It was a diploma project at HEAD Geneva and received an Honorary Mention at the S+T+ARTS Prize 2024.

title: Maria CHOIR
summary: An interactive installation in which a synthetic reproduction of singer Maria Arnal's voice, produced by models trained on her voice, harmonises in real time with what a visitor sings into a microphone, forming a human-digital choir; an AI-animated avatar responds to the vocal input. Visitors can also record their voice to contribute to a collective synthetic voice model. It was shown in the exhibition AI: Artificial Intelligence at CCCB, Barcelona (18 Oct 2023 – 17 Mar 2024), developed with the Barcelona Supercomputing Center and axolot.cat, and received an Honorary Mention at the S+T+ARTS Prize 2024.

title: MATER NATVRA (FUTURED PAST series)
media: Material / sculpture | Screen / monitor | Network / data
summary: A 1/1 edition in digital and physical form, part of the FUTURED PAST series, commissioned for the Zero 10 section of Art Basel Miami Beach 2025 and shown on the Asprey Studio stand. A digitally sculpted figure of Mother Nature, whose placenta becomes a blind serpent coiled around her leg, was translated into sterling silver by Asprey Studio silversmiths. The digital artwork, issued on a blockchain, is an interactive catalogue in which viewers browse views of the sculpture and a twelve-step creation timeline.

title: Memory Melting
summary: Memory Melting is a light installation by Saad Al-Howede shown outside the stc Metro Station at Noor Riyadh 2025. It consists of three large illuminated forms made from discarded plastic toys collected from children around the world and fused together. Some sources describe the forms as spheres and others as oversized emoji shapes.

title: Memory Orbits
summary: A site-specific installation across the five underground rooms of the Barracks at Nasir Bagh, Lahore, commissioned for Lahore Biennale 03 (2024). Visitors descend into the former air-raid bunkers and pass through objects, ceramic sculptures, a mud-dyed suspended cloth, plant material and light and video projections, including a room with forty images of the sun's phases on the curved wall facing a row of forty wax candles. The work is built around the image of an eclipse.

title: MetaPhase: a contrapuntal dialogue between a pianist and her avatar in the metaverse
media: Performance / body | VR / AR / XR | Sensor / interaction
summary: MetaPhase is an XR piano performance by pianist and researcher Giusy Caruso with the Milan company LWT3, presented at Cremona Musica on 23 September 2022. Wearing a suit with light-reflecting markers, an sEMG biosensor and an Oculus Rift headset, Caruso plays the counterpoint part of Steve Reich's Piano Phase with an avatar pianist animated from her own previously recorded movements and Yamaha Disklavier audio, while her biosignals modify visuals, video effects and audio parameters. The audience watches the virtual scene projected in real time, can choose viewpoints and view the data, and could afterwards experience the performance in VR; it received an Honorary Mention at the S+T+ARTS Prize 2023.

title: Micro-Nano Landscape
summary: A video work built from high-magnification microscope recordings of magnetically controlled micro-nano robotic collectives: magnetic microparticles that, under a dual-axis oscillating magnetic field, self-assemble into clusters, grow, tilt and move together. The footage, which the catalogue states is not animated or simulated, is enlarged to projection scale and presented as landscape- and calligraphy-like imagery. Made by Suxuan Jiang with research collaboration from Jiangfan Yu and support from the Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Society (AIRS) SciArt Co-lab; Honorary Mention, New Animation Art, Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Mid Tide #3
summary: A silent three-channel video installation (48:49 seamless loop) made from three and a half hours of fixed-camera 4K 120fps footage of waves breaking against rocks as the light and tide change. Furusawa's own software turns the footage into a 3D object with time as its depth and cuts it along freely moving planes instead of the usual front-to-back playback, so different moments appear side by side within one frame. Viewers watch the waves keep their form while the rocks appear to metamorphose.

title: Midéegaadi
media: Screen / monitor | Performance / body | Material / sculpture
summary: Midéegaadi is a series of videos in which Cannupa Hanska Luger wears bison regalia made from repurposed materials and dances to call bison back onto the land, enacting a Northern Plains ancestral practice. In April 2025 it was shown as a multi-channel presentation on more than 92 electronic billboards in Times Square nightly from 11:57pm to midnight as a Midnight Moment commission with For Freedoms, with a live performance by Mali Obomsawin and Deerlady on 11 April. It is part of the artist's ongoing speculative fiction project Future Ancestral Technologies.

title: Mnemosyne
summary: A 35-minute immersive work that combines VR film (360° animation and 180° live-action footage) with live theatre performance and an installation environment of meditation booths, inspired by Tang Xianzu's Ming Dynasty play The Peony Pavilion. Audience members wear headsets inside the installation and, near the end, meet a live actor with mixed reality elements. It was shown in the Future Cinema section of the Shanghai International Film Festival (2025) and out of competition in the Biennale College Cinema – Immersive section of Venice Immersive 2025.

title: Moving Earth, Crossing Water, Eating Soil
summary: A multipart mixed-media installation on St John's Island (Pulau Sekijang Bendera), Singapore, commissioned for Singapore Biennale 2022 (Natasha), with performances and activations. In the island's main administrative building a four-pillared structure based on the Javanese saka guru holds a shrine-like arrangement of objects referring to the island's history, with painted cutouts of eight animals from Bugis divination diagrams; visitors follow nine archetypal symbols (The Guide, The Witness, The Wrathful Deity and others). In the garden, eight wind-driven wooden instruments strike bamboo plates, and visitors can also turn them by hand.

title: Moving Parts
summary: A sound and video exhibition built from field recordings and footage made on Lagos bridges, especially pedestrian bridges, installed across multiple screens in Odeya Carpark, Onikan, Lagos Island, in November 2025. Visitors move through the audio-visual installation; on the opening day the artist performed the score live with double bass, percussion and flutes.

title: Máquinas Salvajes
media: Robotics / kinetics | Material / sculpture | Sensor / interaction
summary: Máquinas Salvajes (Wild Machines) consists of biodegradable mechanical sculptures with wooden skeletons and biopolymer skins (agar-agar and gelatin) made from materials of Costa Rican ecosystems. Two were left in the Sarapiquí rainforest and in Orotina to decay or be eaten, which was documented on video; in the exhibition (Lentos Museum, Linz, 2023) the videos are shown with a third sculpture that a sensor sprays with water when visitors are present, gradually degrading it. The project received a 2023 CIFO-Ars Electronica Award.

title: Night Charades
summary: Night Charades is a silent AI-generated animation commissioned for the LED facade of the M+ museum in Hong Kong, shown nightly from 22 March to 29 June 2025. Animated characters mime around 50 scenes, gestures and poses from 1980s and 1990s Hong Kong cinema, re-enacting roles originally played by actors such as Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung and Chow Yun-fat. An algorithm continuously reshuffles the scenes and characters into new combinations, viewed by passers-by across Victoria Harbour.

title: No Bird
media: Robotics / kinetics | Sensor / interaction | Material / sculpture
summary: A kinetic installation (265 x 265 x 150 cm) on a sand surface with two machines: a bird-like walking machine that leaves bird footprints in the sand, and a trace-erasing machine following behind that scratches out the tracks with a toothbrush, smooths them with a wire rake and flattens the surface with soft bristles. According to designboom, the movement is triggered by a sensor when a viewer comes close and runs for about two minutes while the viewer stays in range. The duo (Yoo Byoung-Joon and Lim Hee-Young, Seoul) received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: NoSearchBar
summary: NoSearchBar is a Chrome browser extension that removes the search bar from every website, including search engines such as google.com, and changes the browser's search provider so that searching from the URL address bar is disabled. A user who installs it can only reach content through what websites offer without a search, such as categories, sorting, forecasts and recommendation systems. It was made in the New Media Class at UdK Berlin (winter 2021) and received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art+ at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Nothing to See Here
media: Camera / computer vision | Sound | Sensor / interaction
summary: Nothing to See Here is an interactive viewing box by Celine Daemen and Studio Nergens, installed in public spaces such as train stations. A visitor looks through stereoscopic spyholes in a mirrored cube and sees a live 3D image of themselves from above, peering into the box, while fictional figures (a confused man, a wolf, a plastic bag) and a spatial soundscape act around this double. A prototype was shown at Cultura Nova in Heerlen station in 2025 and the world premiere was at IDFA DocLab in November 2025.

title: Now You See Me, Now You Don't
summary: An installation of 12 trampolines set flush into a desert valley near AlUla to resemble puddles, commissioned for the first Desert X AlUla (2020) and since on permanent display. Visitors can touch, lie on and jump on them; after dark the trampolines are lit and change in appearance as people interact with them. The work addresses water scarcity in Saudi Arabia.

title: Nuestra Victoria (Our Victory)
media: Camera / computer vision | Screen / monitor | Online / net art
summary: A series of works built on a 3D digital archive of Mexico City's Angel of Independence monument. Gil documented the monument with drone footage and photogrammetry after feminist protests against violence towards women in August 2019, before it was boarded up and restored. The record is shown as video (in one installation on two 55-inch screens, commissioned for Storefront TV) and as photographic prints, and the 3D files can be downloaded.

title: Nyctinasty
summary: A black-and-white single-channel film of about 7 minutes 54 seconds in which the artist, as protagonist, carries out an evening routine of cleansing and self-care alone in a modernist house before nightfall, as unseen presences gather. It borrows the pacing of horror cinema and draws on Aboriginal practices of caring for body and spirit after death. It was commissioned by the National Gallery of Australia for the 4th National Indigenous Art Triennial: Ceremony (2022).

title: Oceans in Transformation
summary: Oceans in Transformation is a three-year research project by Territorial Agency (John Palmesino and Ann-Sofi Rönnskog), commissioned by TBA21–Academy, that assembles satellite remote-sensing, bathymetric, fishing, shipping and climate data into large dynamic image compositions of the changing world ocean. It was shown as an exhibition at Ocean Space, Church of San Lorenzo, Venice (2020–2021), released online in seven trajectories on Ocean Archive with essays co-edited with e-flux Architecture, and accompanied by 'Messy Studio' gatherings with scientists, activists and policymakers. It won the S+T+ARTS Prize 2021 Grand Prize for Artistic Exploration.

title: Octopocalypse
summary: Octopocalypse is an immersive installation for three participants, who enter an interrogation room after a fictional meteor storm and face an alien octopus that communicates through music, touch, rhythm and visions. With questions, button presses and rhythm the group shapes the outcome and builds a music track from impulses sent by the alien, choosing whether to interrogate it or earn its trust. It premiered in the Venice Immersive competition in 2026; the makers say they used generative AI as a production tool.

title: Of Men and Gods and Mud
summary: A three-channel video installation shown at the 59th Venice Biennale (The Milk of Dreams), where Cherri received the Silver Lion for a Promising Young Participant. Shot mainly at a brickyard near the Merowe Dam on the Nile in northern Sudan, it follows a seasonal brickmaker who shapes mud into bricks by day and at night secretly builds a structure of mud and scrap that becomes a creature. It was shown alongside drawings of mud creatures and three sculptural figures, Titans.

title: Oikeiōsis
summary: Oikeiōsis is a two-room installation by Pavlina Vagioni at Spazio Tana, Venice, presented by the Hellenic Diaspora Foundation during the 61st Biennale Arte (6 May - 25 October 2026). In the first room, Neikos, a polygonal plexiglass cube reflects visitors in fragmented form; in the second, Philotes, six rock-salt seats surround a hexagonal mirrored structure, and when visitors sit, sound and light respond, building a layered vocal soundscape that includes the artist's soprano voice. The salt seats change shape over the exhibition through visitors' touch.

title: On a Clear Day You Can See Forever
summary: A two-channel video installation (synchronised rear HD projections, colour, four-channel sound, 39 min) on translucent voile screens held in a parallel, trapezoid frame, shown in a shop unit at Lucky Plaza, Orchard Road, for Singapore Biennale 2025. One screen shows Inuka, Singapore's first polar bear born in captivity, circling in his zoo enclosure; the other shows 80km/h (2004), a single-take drive along the Pan Island Expressway filmed from the passenger seat at a constant 80 km/h. Visitors view the two projections overlapping through the frame.

title: Once Upon a Garden
summary: An ongoing series (begun 2021, first shown as a special project commissioned by ART X Lagos in 2022) in which the artist trained a GAN, and later diffusion and video models, on records of extinct and critically endangered flora from the Sahel region of West Africa to generate images of these plants. In the first chapter the generated flowers were curated, animated and composited into artificial gardens installed at exhibitions; the complete series (2022–2024) presents 50 speculative flora across five chapters.

title: Ongoing, Individual Adaptability or How to Quiet Quit
summary: A two-part web work commissioned for the Whitney Museum's artport, made with a generative adversarial network (GAN) trained on thousands of installation photographs of Whitney exhibitions. The first part, Ongoing, Individual Adaptability, shows twelve GAN images collaged with manipulated excerpts of artist correspondence and ephemera from the Whitney's library; the second, How to Quiet Quit, is three videos of the GAN producing images, with soundtracks of TED-talk excerpts by Nick Bostrom, Kai-Fu Lee and Janelle Shane interrupted by the artist's comments and questions. Visitors change the sequence of images and videos by refreshing the page; the title quotes Octavia E. Butler's Parable of the Sower.

title: OPERA
summary: An 8K animation conceived as an installation: a looping cycle of about five minutes showing a giant pyramid filled with hundreds of small black-and-white figures in a hierarchical society, passing through day and night, modelled on Renaissance fresco murals. The installation version has no dialogue and no camera movement; visitors walk along the image and choose which characters and sections to follow. A cinema version was nominated for the 2021 Academy Award for Animated Short Film, and the work received an Award of Distinction in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: Pandemonium
media: Projection | VR / AR / XR | Robotics / kinetics
summary: A multimedia project that premiered in October 2025 at Moore College of Art & Design and the Fels Planetarium at The Franklin Institute, Philadelphia. It combines mechatronics, animation and sound with a 360-degree film shown with 8K projection in the planetarium dome, and the opening performance used a robot. The film shows a tornado of debris, including newspaper clippings swirling out of a tornado machine built by the artist; at the 2026 Whitney Biennial it was shown on a 20-ft circular screen overhead (approx. 20 min.).

title: Paper Tears
summary: An installation of light, sound, choreography and image for Catalonia in Venice, a collateral event of the 61st Venice Biennale (Docks Cantieri Cucchini, 9 May–22 November 2026), curated by Elise Lammer for the Institut Ramon Llull. Four lasers project 15th-century paper watermarks from the archive of the Museu Molí Paperer de Capellades, a sculptural LED screen shows drone footage of four aquifer springs, and performers dressed as jesters deliver monologues in a script structured like a waltz, with a soundtrack. Visitors walk around and onto platforms to change their point of view.

title: Pinktoned (Exploded View)
summary: A multi-screen installation shown in its own room at the Hammer Museum's Made in L.A. 2025. It presents the component parts of Stoltz's 16mm film Pinktoned separately: footage of passersby filmed from his East Hollywood studio, faded 1976 slides of Los Angeles streets wheat-pasted with posters for the documentary Underground, and a black-and-white moving graphic. A third screen runs a 16mm optical soundtrack of 'pink tone' test frequencies on a loop, and visitors see the street footage and the slides across the room from each other.

title: Pixel Dust
summary: Pixel Dust is a video of pulsating particles made with the artist's custom software, premiered as Times Square Arts' Midnight Moment for November 2025. It played synchronized on over 90 electronic billboards in Times Square nightly from 11:57pm to midnight, November 1-30, 2025.

title: PL'AI
media: Robotics / kinetics | AI / generative | Camera / computer vision
summary: An installation lasting several months in which cucumber plants grown from seed and an AI-controlled robot about three metres tall interact. The robot moves 36 bouncy balls on stainless steel threads above a tray of plants; a camera and a 3D scanner (scanning every 15 minutes) feed the AI, and when a plant's tendril grabs a ball, that ball stops moving. Produced in 2020 by Kersnikova Institute / Kapelica Gallery (European ARTificial Intelligence Lab), it received an Honorary Mention at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: Pocket Money
summary: Pocket Money is a video work of about 15 minutes, shot between September and December 2025, featuring about 20 young people from in and around Adelaide in their first paid jobs, such as fast food and shelf-stacking, as well as at rest in their bedrooms, spending money and pursuing hobbies. It was shown in the 2026 Adelaide Biennial of Australian Art: Yield Strength (27 February – 8 June 2026).

title: Pollinator Pathmaker
media: AI / generative | Online / net art | Material / sculpture
summary: An algorithmic garden-design tool and website (pollinator.art) that generates planting designs computed to support the greatest number of pollinator species, choosing from curated regional plant palettes. Users select their garden conditions, receive a unique design they can explore in 3D or with a 'pollinator vision' view, and download planting instructions with an edition certificate; each planted garden is an edition of the work. Commissioned Editions have been planted at the Eden Project, Cornwall (2022), for the Serpentine in Kensington Gardens, London, and outside the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin (LAS Art Foundation); it won the S+T+ARTS Grand Prize 2023.

title: Prometheus Firebringer
summary: Prometheus Firebringer is a lecture-performance of about an hour on generative AI, technology and power. On one side of the stage, a chorus of AI-generated Greek masks with AI-generated voices performs a new version each night of the lost final play of Aeschylus' Prometheia trilogy, generated by a GPT language model; on the other side, Dorsen delivers a talk composed entirely of passages quoted from other texts. It premiered at Bryn Mawr College in January 2023 and was then presented at The Chocolate Factory, Theatre for a New Audience and REDCAT.

title: puberty
summary: puberty is an installation commissioned for the Simon Lee Foundation Institute of Contemporary Asian Art at the Art Gallery of Western Australia, shown in the gallery foyer from 22 July to 11 December 2022. It combines animation on an iPad with cast acrylic, chain, fans and synthetic turf, forming a face whose eyes, nose, tongue and mouth are described by the venue as moving elements.

title: Quando o segundo Sol chegar / Um cometa nos teus olhos
summary: A two-channel video installation, the third film of a trilogy made on the Transamazônica highway (BR-230), shown in MASP's Video Room. It shows scenes of the highway under a fleeting glow that suggests a 'second Sun' approaching Earth, set against a text that tells a physical and existential journey. The project began during a residency at the Centro Cultural do Cariri awarded at the 22nd Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil.

title: Quine
media: AI / generative | Network / data | Text / print
summary: Quine is a generative series of 497 blockchain-based artworks by Larva Labs (Matt Hall and John Watkinson), released on October 9, 2025 as the final Art Blocks Curated project. Each work's image contains the source code of the program that generates it, laid out on a grid; some outputs reproduce themselves exactly while others cycle through several generations, and collectors can choose which generation to display. At Zero 10, Art Basel Miami Beach 2025, all 497 works were shown in miniature on a vitrine table, with 10 shown as signed, framed works.

title: RADIO GHOST
summary: Radio Ghost is an audio-driven, app-based walking game for three players set in a shopping centre, part game, part interactive radio show and part ghost hunt. Players act as ghost hunters, following audio prompts on phones and blending in as shoppers to unlock stories of the mall connected to the supply chains of the goods on sale. It was commissioned by LIFT Festival 2022 and won the Lumen Prize Interactive Award 2022.

title: Raster und Spectrum
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: Raster und Spectrum is an onchain abstract real-time animation that can play on any device, shown by Nguyen Wahed in the Zero 10 section of Art Basel Miami Beach 2025. Two brushes — a raster of white lines on black and a spectrum that continuously cycles through hues — cross the screen in one of eight directions and return when they meet an edge.

title: Re: cite, member, sist
summary: Re: cite, member, sist is a site-specific installation with textile, 4-channel sound and found material, commissioned for Colomboscope 2026 (Rhythm Alliances) and shown at Colpetty Town House, Colombo. According to the festival publication it combines layered cyanotypes, shadow drawings referencing early illustrations of Portuguese colonial exploits, tracings of the artist's grandmother's embroidery patterns on cushions, curtains and household objects, and sound recordings of ocean tides and dialogues with her aunt. It draws on the artist's family's Goan history and her grandmother's migration from Bardez to Karachi.

title: Reality Looks Back
summary: A 21-minute dome documentary, world-premiered in the IDFA DocLab Competition for Immersive Non-Fiction in 2025 and shown in the DocLab Exhibition and at the Planetarium, directed by Anne Jeppesen with co-director Omid Zarei (Superposition XR Studio). Jeppesen's narration moves through quantum observation, split déjà vu, parallel realities and the death of her elderly hamster Oliver, over documentary footage processed into Gaussian splats. The work began as an audio piece made in the YASS! mentorship programme (Lucia Festival / Radio Papesse), premiered in Florence in 2024.

title: Regular Animals
media: Robotics / kinetics | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: Regular Animals is an installation of autonomous robot dogs fitted with hyper-realistic silicone heads of figures including Andy Warhol, Pablo Picasso, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos and Beeple himself, which move around a glass-walled pen using LIDAR to avoid each other. The robots take pictures of their surroundings, reinterpret them with AI in the style associated with each character, and print them out of their rear; some of the prints carry QR codes to claim NFTs. It was first shown at Art Basel Miami Beach's Zero 10 section in December 2025 and later at the Neue Nationalgalerie, Berlin, in 2026.

title: REPETAE
summary: A series of language artworks combining AI-generated text, code-based visuals sketched in p5.js, and digitally looped and layered spoken word, presented as standalone works and longer interconnected cycles built around repetition. Parts include a browser-based piece that generates a new line of poetry every few minutes from the mantra WORDS CAN COMMUNICATE BEYOND WORDS. It received a Prix Ars Electronica 2024 Award of Distinction (AI in ART) and was shown as REPETAE: Again, Again at the Lentos Museum, Linz.

title: Requiem for an Exit
summary: An installation centred on a four-metre-tall armless robotic figure on a steel and hydraulic structure, whose hyperrealistic face is a projected animation built from a motion-capture recording of Thomas Kvam. In a darkened room with multichannel sound, the robot delivers a monologue written by the artists and voiced with AI speech synthesis, tracing genocide through human history from the disappearance of the Neanderthals; there is no interactivity. First shown at Meta.Morf 2024 in Trondheim (co-produced by TEKS); Golden Nica, New Animation Art, Prix Ars Electronica 2025.

title: Rhythmic Ramp
summary: Rhythmic Ramp (Rampa rítmica) is a site-specific work by Cevdet Erek on the external ramp of Oscar Niemeyer's Ciccillo Matarazzo Pavilion at the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, the ramp that connects the exhibition's floors. It combines sonic and geometric elements placed along the ramp. Its sound includes rhythmic patterns drawn from music undergrounds in Istanbul and from São Paulo's vernacular rhythms, and visitors and passersby meet it as they go up and down the ramp.

title: Ri-lancia Luigi Broglio (Re-launching Luigi Broglio)
summary: Ri-lancia Luigi Broglio is a 33-minute 360° VR film directed by Vincenzo Cavallo, staged like a theatre piece, about Luigi Broglio, who launched Italy into space from the San Marco sea platform off Kenya in the 1960s. The viewer watches a confrontation between Broglio and a journalist in the abandoned command centre, with flashbacks to the African expedition, an encounter with Enrico Mattei and a near-diplomatic crisis with President Nasser. It was supported by Biennale College Cinema Immersive and shown out of competition at Venice Immersive 2025.

title: Résonances
summary: Résonances is an interactive installation in which a visitor's gestures return as a visual and sound echo: earlier actions resurface and overlap with present ones, so the visitor can choreograph the present on top of their own past. It was unveiled in December 2021 in the CORPS DATA exhibition at Îlot Balmoral in Montreal with ELEKTRA, and shown at the 6th International Digital Art Biennial (BIAN) at Arsenal Contemporary Art Montreal; an outdoor edition was presented at i Light Singapore 2023 and Future Media FEST 2024 in Taipei.

title: Sange Khara [Hard Stone]
summary: Sange Khara [Hard Stone] is an installation developed for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, anchored by a looping 16mm film of desert and oasis landscapes and figures drawn from cinematic references. Visitors sit or lie down under a tent-like canopy of melhifa cloth, a fabric worn by women in the Sahara, in a scenography based on nomadic structures of southern Morocco, surrounded by sound and light. It is a chapter of Hida's ongoing project Le Voyage du Phénix.

title: Satan in America and Other Invisible Evils: Experiments in Public Sculpture (Witches 1–3)
summary: Three witch figures in an installation shown at the Whitney Biennial 2026 that draws on scenes from American history, from the Salem witch trials to Abraham Lincoln's birth near Hodgenville, Kentucky. The witches' bodies are built from open-source medical 3D CT scans of human bodies, and two Salem villagers nearby are built from character models taken from the video game Doom. Visitors walk among figures mounted on metal poles alongside the artist's Symbolic Birth Cabin Unit and two demon figures.

title: Screen Melancholy
media: Screen / monitor | Material / sculpture | AI / generative
summary: Screen Melancholy (2026) is a video installation by Li Yi-Fan, presented by the Taipei Fine Arts Museum as Taiwan's collateral event at the 61st Venice Biennale in the Palazzo delle Prigioni, curated by Raphael Fonseca. In the video, Li performs a monologue through a game-engine digital character in the tone of an online tutorial, addressing subscription-based image software and AI-generated images. Large sculptures of fragmented limbs are placed throughout the space; visitors can sit on them and charge their phones from chargers built into the sculptures.

title: Skeleton of the Glorious
summary: Skeleton of the Glorious is a light installation by Khalid Zahid in the gardens of the King Abdulaziz Historical Center for Noor Riyadh 2025. It is a hollow, wireframe-like structure based on Al-Masmak Fort, the adobe and clay citadel of old Riyadh. It is lit from within, so the inner form is visible while the exterior falls into shadow.

title: SKY/WORLD DEATH/WORLD
media: Online / net art | Text / print | Screen / monitor
summary: A two-part Whitney artport commission for the Sunrise/Sunset series (Dec 2022–Apr 2023) that played on whitney.org at sunrise and sunset in New York. SKY/WORLD pairs game-engine animations of dawn, drawing on the Haudenosaunee story of Sky Woman, with the question "Who benefits from your burnout?"; DEATH/WORLD pairs abstract visuals and video of the artist recovered from the Internet Archive with "What is made bright by the loss of your light?". Viewers can click a switch to change the animation while answering text populates the screen.

title: SMOG SEASON
media: Sensor / interaction | Robotics / kinetics | Network / data
summary: SMOG SEASON is an installation of 80 cigarette packs mounted on 5 motor-driven circular bases, using Bangkok PM 2.5 air-pollution data and the cigarette-equivalence figure from Berkeley Earth (one cigarette per 22 micrograms per cubic meter per day). Visitors scan a QR code, choose a smoke level on their smartphone and hold it to a light sensor; the bases spin and lights blink at 18 FPS so the cigarette-label pictures appear animated, while an LED display shows the date, time and PM 2.5 value. It received an Honorary Mention in Prix Ars Electronica 2023 (New Animation Art).

title: Smoke and Mirrors
summary: A 4m30s data animation based on NASA's Blue Marble photograph: a counter shows atmospheric methane in parts per billion from 1970 to the present while the rotating globe fills with pink smoke, and advertising slogans from the oil industry (e.g. "Out to clean the air", "Unsettled Science", "Doomsday is cancelled") appear across the screen at their dates. It is set to the song "Oh My Heart" and was produced with the studio Parliament, using NOAA, NASA and EEA data. It received the Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica (New Animation Art) in 2024 and has been shown as a video and in exhibitions.

title: Soft Collision
